newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marubeni officials in Iraq for oil talks.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni officials in Iraq for oil talks.

text.p: Marubeni Corp is currently negotiating with Iraq for the possible purchase of crude oil, a company official said on Wednesday.
"Our staff from the oil department arrived in Baghdad over the weekend to discuss possible crude purchases and to gather information," a spokesman for the trading house said.
He declined to say how much crude the company planned to buy. "Talks with Iraq are still in progress," he said.
Japanese trading houses such as Mitsubishi Corp, which will act as an agent for about five Japanese oil firms, and Itochu Corp have also sent officials to Baghdad to discuss crude purchases.
Iraq on Tuesday began pumping crude oil through its pipeline to the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan for the first time since August 1990 when a United Nations embargo was imposed.
A U.N. partial oil sales plan will allow it to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil to buy food and medicine.
Iraq, the second-biggest OPEC producer after Saudi Arabia before the Gulf War, produced 3.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude in July 1990, a month before it invaded Kuwait.
Japan was a major buyer of Iraqi crude with imports of about 190,000 bpd.
